learning: Baseline only. After the first race, check whether line_loss_events and steering_oscillation point to sensor dead zones (line_loss) or lead-induced jitter (oscillation), and tune kp, kd and base_speed accordingly.
notes: Baseline integration with a moderate controller and no race data yet. Gains are deliberately conservative so that the first race shows whether the geometry itself, not aggressive tuning, limits performance.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback to act on. I used the Builder's supplied geometry unchanged, because every field is inside its contract range: five sensors at x = -0.02 to 0.02 with y = 0.05, sensor_size 0.012, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12, body_length 0.14, mass 0.7. The controller is built from the contract physics. Sensor weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) follow the sign convention: positive x is left and positive signal steers left, so a line to the left of centre gives a positive signal and the robot turns left. base_speed 1.5 gives PWM fraction 0.75, which should hold the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. kp 4 gives a moderate steering authority (a full signal of 2 produces about 2800 PWM of differential). ki 0.2 is kept small to avoid integral windup on the S-bend. kd 0.3 damps the lead-sensor response. line_loss is last_direction, so the robot keeps turning the way it was going when it leaves the tape. The observation request covers completion, progress, time, rms and max error, line-loss count, oscillation and controller errors, so the Builder and I can separate tracking error from jitter.
